messages:
dmitri: Quick RFC follow-up - proposing an on-demand staging warmup policy (soft warmup + async pin). Want a short check-in on tradeoffs before I file a small PR.

sana: curious, what do you mean by soft warmup? prefetch behavior / size? per-tenant limits?

dmitri: soft = prefetch a small prefix of pages (non-blocking) and enqueue an async pin job that completes when pages are resident. If pin fails or GPU under pressure we fall back to cold-path. default prefetch: 4 pages (~64KB) or first N KV segments.

leo: how do we prevent noisy tenants from gaming warmup to hog staging? sounds like a DOS vector.

dmitri: agree - plan is warmup budget per-tenant per-epoch + warmup_priority tokens that are preemptible. warmup requests increment tenant.warmup_usage; deny when >budget.

maria: we'll need metrics: warmup_attempts, warmup_success_rate, warmup_cost_tokens, impact_on_p95_latency. Also a tracing span for warmup lifecycle.

jules: implementation Q: where does the warmup live? pagefault handler, admission controller, or runtime task queue? atomic reservation needed so evictor doesn't immediately reclaim.

dmitri: plan: admission controller triggers prefetch and writes a reservation token into page metadata. eviction checks token and treats it as preemptible reservation. if eviction forced, token cleared. That keeps logic outside hot-path fault handler.

jules: sample config sketch:
```json
{
  "warmup": {
    "enabled": true,
    "prefetch_pages": 4,
    "max_concurrent_warmups": 64,
    "tenant_budget_tokens": 5000,
    "reservation_ttl_ms": 30000
  }
}
```

sana: +1. also we should have two modes: `eager` (blocking, used only for pinned dedicated jobs) and `background` (soft warmup). default = background.

leo: backpressure model: warmup tasks must be preemptible. if node GPU free < watermark, cancel warmups and decrement tenant.warmup_usage. otherwise warmup will worsen p95.

maria: can we tie fallback automatically to model variant? e.g., if warmup can't finish, route to smaller/quantized variant instead of blocking. reduces tail latencies for customers.

dmitri: yes, routing policy already supports fallback variants. We'll add a warmup-aware fallback: prefer faster quantized variant if warmup fails or eviction occurs during request.

jules: telemetry detail: define what counts as success. my vote: success = prefetched pages remain resident for at least `reservation_ttl_ms` and first inference sees resident pages within X ms. record `warmup_latency_ms` and `evicted_during_warmup` flag.

maria: add `warmup_cost_tokens` too (how many tokens/bytes spent prefetching). we'll need billing guardrails if cost gets large.

dmitri: agreed. Proposed action items: 1) add config keys + admission hook (owner: @jules), 2) eviction token semantics + evictor check (owner: @leo), 3) metrics and traces (owner: @maria), 4) tenant budget + quota enforcement (owner: @sana). I'll open PR with minimal changes that wire warmup_background=true + metrics.

infra-bot: deploybot: config patch deployed to staging (warmup.enabled=true) — started canary on 3 nodes :rocket:

sana: I'd like a quick A/B on customer-facing perf: enable warmup for 10% of requests on staging, measure p50/p95 change and warmup cost.

dmitri: will do. Can we also gate by `request.size >= some_threshold` so we don't warmup tiny requests?

jules: yes. add `min_request_tokens` in config.

leo: one more thought — warmup should avoid interfering with KV cache warming we do on replay. maybe share the same reservation token namespace so we don't double-count.

dmitri: good call. we'll reuse reservation token object with `source: warmup|replay` field.

maria: I'll add dashboards: warmup_attempts, success_rate, cost_tokens, evicted_during_warmup, p95_delta.

dmitri: cool. timeline: PR today for admission hook + stubs, follow-up for evictor semantics + metrics next week. Owners assigned above. Anyone opposed?

sana: nope. :thumbsup:

leo: +1

jules: +1

maria: +1

dmitri: thanks all — I'll post the PR link here when ready.
